nuclearIntegrity.label: nuclear mechanical integrity
nuclearIntegrity.why_no_term: searched 'nuclear mechanical integrity', 'nuclear envelope integrity', 'nuclear stiffness', 'nuclear fragility', 'nuclear envelope maintenance', 'nuclear lamina', 'nucleus organization', GO 'nuclear envelope', PATO 'stiffness' and 'fragility': GO has nuclear envelope organization (GO:0006998) and nucleus organization (GO:0006997), processes rather than the nucleus's mechanical integrity; PATO has fragility (PATO:0001662), the antonym, which would need a sign change the run never made; MP:0008890 is lamina morphology. Kind phenotype because integrity is a quality of the nucleus; the run types it as a process

abnormalTtnIsoforms.label: abnormal titin (TTN) isoform expression from mis-splicing of TTN
abnormalTtnIsoforms.why_no_term: searched 'abnormal mRNA splicing', 'abnormal RNA splicing', 'alternative splicing', 'titin', 'isoform', MP and HP 'splicing' / 'RNA splicing', UPHENO 'mRNA splicing': HP has none, MP only 'abnormal splicing factor domain morphology'; the abnormal-splicing terms are fission yeast (FYPO) or zebrafish (ZP); UPHENO:0051282 'alternative mRNA splicing, via spliceosome phenotype' (changed alternative splicing of any gene) exists but cannot be restricted to TTN, and TTN is the point of the step. No term names titin isoforms

the run's contradicting citation for h3: a null GWAS result for RBM20 variants and DCM; it bears on h3's claim (RBM20 variants -> DCM), but no step of the run states that link (the chain goes through abnormal TTN isoforms), so it refutes no statement

h1.note: claim 1 is the title's ('LMNA mutations cause DCM'); claim 2 starts where the chain starts (LMNA protein), with the sign the mechanism gives: variants 'disrupt nuclear lamina structural integrity', so lamin A/C function protects. Both are kept although v2 asks for one claim per gene, because the chain's only disease step (h1.2) starts at the variants. h1.1 (LMNA -> nuclear mechanical integrity) is now a statement but leads nowhere, so claim 2 has no route

h2.note: claims 1-3 are the title's ('MYH7, TTN, and TNNT2 mutations ... cause DCM'); h2.2 'sarcomere gene variants' is split per gene because the mechanism defines the set as MYH7, TTN, TNNT2. Claims 4-6 start where the chain starts ('MYH7, TNNT2, TTN proteins', h2.1), read per gene and with the sign the mechanism gives: mutations 'disrupt the assembly or function of the contractile apparatus', so each protein's function protects. h2.1 is now six statements (three genes x sarcomere organization, muscle contraction), but no step leads from either process to DCM, so claims 4-6 have no route

h3.note: claim 1 is the title's ('RBM20 mutations ... cause DCM'); claim 2 starts where the chain starts (RBM20), with the sign the mechanism gives: variants 'disrupt its normal function'. Claim 1 has no route: h3.2 ('leads to abnormal TTN isoform expression') is an undirected change with no HP or MP term, so it is unexpressed (no_sign), and h3.3 (abnormal isoforms -> DCM) is reached by no statement; h3.3 has no evidence anyway. Claim 2 has no route: h3.1 ends at alternative splicing, which is not the abnormal-isoform node

findings.detail: every chain opens with 'gene required_for its normal function' (h1.1, h2.1, h3.1) that no later step uses; h1 and h2 then jump straight from variants to DCM (h1.2, h2.2), h3 goes variants -> abnormal TTN isoforms -> DCM (h3.2, h3.3), and h2 and h3 end with an 'associated_with cardiomyocytes' expression step (h2.3, h3.4); so the named mechanisms (nuclear integrity, sarcomere assembly) sit beside the disease steps rather than in a chain
h1.1 ends at 'nuclear mechanical integrity', h1.2 starts at 'LMNA variants'; nothing links nuclear integrity (the title's 'nuclear lamina disruption') to DCM
h2.1 ends at 'sarcomere assembly and contraction', h2.2 starts at 'sarcomere gene variants'; the title's 'sarcomere assembly disruption impairs contractility' has no step to DCM
h3.1 ends at 'TTN splicing', h3.2 starts at 'RBM20 variants'

h3.2 ends at 'abnormal TTN isoform expression' (kind process), h3.3 starts at 'abnormal TTN splicing'; same node, different labels (h3.3's own note says 'Abnormal TTN isoforms'), merged here; the link still does not compose because h3.2 is an undirected change and is unexpressed (no_sign)

the step's note reports what the two papers found (metabolic and proliferation pathway changes in R541C iPSC cardiomyocytes; AAV lamin A rescue of cardiac dysfunction in Lmna-/- mice), neither of which is 'LMNA variants lead to DCM'; only PMID:42373902's background sentence states the step, and PMID:PPR1285401's title only says the variant is 'associated with' DCM

'sarcomere gene variants' covers MYH7, TTN and TNNT2, but every citation (NEJM TTN truncations, three TTN-locus GWAS rows) is about TTN; the MYH7 and TNNT2 arms have no supporting evidence, only the run's own GWAS null results against them

cites three common TTN-locus GWAS SNPs as support for disease-causing variants; for rs16866400-A and rs12988307-C the reported allele lowers DCM liability (beta decrease) and rs2042995's risk allele T is the common allele (0.78), so the rows say nothing about rare pathogenic mutations

TNNT2's UniProt text gives a regulatory role (calcium sensitivity of actomyosin ATPase), not a requirement for sarcomere assembly or contraction; MYH7's text supports contraction, not assembly; TTN's supports assembly, but says 'functioning', elasticity and force balance, not contraction. Of the six gene x process parts, two have support
cites PMID:22335739 (TTN truncating mutations cause DCM) for 'abnormal TTN splicing / isoforms lead to DCM'; truncation is not an isoform shift. The only step that carries h3 to DCM has no support

PMID:PPR1251737 is a deep mutational scan of RBM20 localization and splicing function and never mentions TTN; the only support for the step is one R634W carrier's explanted myocardium in PMID:42462460
'associated_with cardiomyocytes' steps are HPA expression facts placed in a causal chain; they end the chain at a cell type and add nothing to any route (now rel 'expressed in' statements)
h2 is the only hypothesis rated 'high', yet two of its three genes have no supporting citation and the run's own contradicting_evidence lists GWAS no-association for MYH7 and TNNT2

the four contradicting entries, now fetched, are GWAS Catalog gene-level absences ('no association between any X variant and dilated cardiomyopathy ... among the 66 curated associations'); GWAS arrays do not test the rare pathogenic variants every hypothesis is about, so these barely bear on the claims, while the run cites three common TTN GWAS hits as support for h2.2: GWAS is read as relevant to rare variants when it supports and when it contradicts, and neither is right

h1 and h3 falsifications describe introducing a pathogenic variant but set the perturbation action to 'knockout' / 'knockdown', and read out sarcomere organization / TTN splicing rather than DCM; h2's falsification tests a triple-mutant joint effect although the title claims each gene separately

the run types variant classes ('LMNA variants', 'sarcomere gene variants', 'RBM20 variants') as kind 'gene', 'TTN splicing' as kind 'gene', and 'abnormal TTN isoform expression' as a process; only DCM and RBM20 carry CURIEs
Europe PMC preprint ids are written 'PMID:PPR1285401' and 'PMID:PPR1251737'; they are not PMIDs (render.py now renders them as records with pmid 0)
ABCB9 and OR8J3 were left in unexplained_genes rather than forced into a hypothesis

'LMNA variants', 'sarcomere gene variants' and 'RBM20 variants' name unspecified variant classes with no identifier (no ClinVar set, no allele); recorded as BLN:LMNA-, BLN:TTN-, BLN:MYH7-, BLN:TNNT2- and BLN:RBM20-pathogenic-variants

h3.2's own citations state the RBM20 variant to DCM link directly (PMID:42462460 'Mutations in the cardiac splicing factor RNA binding motif protein 20 (RBM20) are associated with severe forms of dilated cardiomyopathy'; PMID:PPR1251737 'the dilated cardiomyopathy (DCM)-associated protein RBM20'), a step the chain lacks; the chain instead reaches DCM only through 'abnormal TTN splicing' (h3.3), which it supports with a TTN-truncation paper

no term for nuclear mechanical integrity (or nuclear stiffness / nuclear envelope integrity); GO has only nuclear envelope organization and PATO only the antonym fragility; made BLN:NuclearMechanicalIntegrity (kind phenotype, a quality, where the run says process)

no term for abnormal titin isoform expression / abnormal TTN splicing; HP and MP have no abnormal-splicing phenotype, only FYPO and ZP do, and UPHENO:0051282 (changed alternative splicing, any gene) cannot be restricted to TTN; made BLN:AbnormalTitinIsoformExpression (phenotype) as the subject of h3.3, but under the undirected-change rule h3.2 ('leads to abnormal X', no HP/MP term) stays unexpressed (no_sign), so h3's variant claim does not compose

the step that carries h3's mechanism, RBM20 variants -> 'abnormal TTN isoform expression', never says which way titin's isoforms shift (the mechanism says only 'abnormal titin isoforms with altered elastic properties', the cited text only 'Aberrant TTN-splicing'), so it cannot be signed and h3's variant claim has no route

the undirected-change rule covers an 'abnormal X' object ('leads to abnormal X': HP/MP term or no_sign) but not an 'abnormal X' subject ('abnormal TTN splicing leads to DCM'), and the BLN rule says to make a term for a missing node; so one node can be a BLN term as h3.3's subject but not as h3.2's object, and the chain breaks between the two

a process restricted to one gene's transcripts (TTN splicing): no ctx field names a target gene, so h3.1 drops TTN and lands on generic alternative mRNA splicing, which cannot meet the BLN abnormal-TTN-isoform node of h3.2/h3.3

no identifier exists for a gene's class of pathogenic variants (ClinVar and dbSNP name single variants, SO only variant types), so the run's variant classes are local terms BLN:LMNA-pathogenic-variants, BLN:TTN-pathogenic-variants, BLN:MYH7-pathogenic-variants, BLN:TNNT2-pathogenic-variants and BLN:RBM20-pathogenic-variants; they cannot meet any other run's node

a background sentence in a mouse paper (review, 3/5) outweighs the NEJM TTN sequencing study (cosegregation lod 11.1, >95% penetrance), which counts only 1/2 because it is observational; human Mendelian segregation evidence has no kind above observational, so the best-supported arm of the run (TTN) ends 'unsupported' at belief 1/2

a GWAS Catalog gene-level 'no association' counts as a full observational refutation (1/2) of a rare-variant Mendelian claim, the weight of a study that tested those variants: the MYH7 and TNNT2 arms end at disbelief 1/2 and the LMNA arm 'contested' (belief 3/7, disbelief 2/7), although GWAS arrays could not have seen the variants; the weight should depend on whether the design could have detected the effect

a contradicting citation that bears on a hypothesis claim (RBM20 variants -> DCM) but on no step of the run has nowhere to attach; it is excluded as 'other' under the nearest step (h3.2, now unexpressed) and never reaches the claim it contradicts
the kind table has no row for an HPA expression record supporting an 'expressed in' rel; used observational (measured single-cell expression)

v2 asks for one claim per gene with the subject where the chain starts (here the protein), but every chain here starts at the protein and reaches DCM only from the variants; one claim per gene would leave h1 and h2 with no route although their variant steps are stated and cited, so both claims are kept

audit.reason: h3.2 is 'leads to abnormal TTN isoform expression' with no direction of the isoform shift in the step, note, mechanism or cited texts. The guide's undirected-change rule is specific: an effect on an 'abnormal X' phenotype only if an HP or MP term exists, 'otherwise it is unexpressed, no_sign'. None exists (only FYPO, ZP, UPHENO). A local BLN 'abnormal X' term sidesteps exactly that rule, and every other curation applies it, including the same RBM20 mis-splicing step in the sibling r2 run (hyp2.1 no_sign). The general BLN rule covers missing nodes, not missing signs
